findings.title: Unindexed fixture example lacks the bold wrap the parser requires
findings.description: Task 1's example unindexed line (`7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.`) has no `**Name**` bold wrap, and its success criterion explicitly requires bold wrap only "for the indexed form", pointing at "the existing line style/format already used by the `[ ]`/`[x]` entries in that file". But the only unindexed line in `sample-slice-plan.md` sits in the skipped "Future Work" section and is unbolded — the parser never consumes it. `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/slicePlanParser.ts:9`) requires `\*\*([^(].*?)\*\*`, so a fixture line copied verbatim from the example matches neither regex and is silently dropped — the exact failure mode this slice exists to fix (and a CLAUDE.md hallucination trap: the nearest plausible token is the wrong format). Slice-design success criterion 2 shows the correct form (`N. [~] **Name** — rationale`), and the production unindexed format in `packages/core/tests/fixtures/introspection/unindexed-slice-plan.md` bold-wraps every name. Task 1 should specify the bolded form for both entries.

findings.title: Shared-fixture fallout is understated; more than one existing assertion breaks
findings.description: Task 1 extends the shared `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture, but Task 5 names only the `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` test as needing update. At least four other assertions in `packages/core/tests/introspection/slicePlanParser.test.ts` and one in `packages/core/tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts` depend on that fixture's exact shape and will break: `slicePlanParser.test.ts:10` (`toHaveLength(5)`), `slicePlanParser.test.ts:12-32` (positional `entries[0]`/`entries[2]` toEqual — the new unindexed entry gets fallback index 1 and sorts before 101, shifting all positions), `slicePlanParser.test.ts:128` (`every indexSource === 'explicit'` — false once the fixture contains a fallback entry), `slicePlanParser.test.ts:166-167` (positional description assertions), and `ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` (`totalSlices).toBe(5)`). This also undermines success criterion 7's proof strategy ("the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture tests continuing to pass unchanged") — the slice design explicitly allowed "(or add a sibling fixture)", which would have preserved that proof. Either name the affected assertions in Task 5 or use a sibling fixture as the design permits.

findings.title: `arch-status-vs-plans` half of the success criterion has no test task
findings.description: Success criterion 6 names both `plan-status-vs-entries` **and** `arch-status-vs-plans` as rules that must not false-positive when a plan's frontmatter is `status: complete` with a `[~]`-only non-checked entry. Task 12 (and the Verification Walkthrough step 5) covers only `plan-status-vs-entries`. `ruleArchStatusVsPlans` (`packages/core/src/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.ts:828-853`) computes the identical `allComplete = completedSlices === totalSlices` predicate and has the identical false-positive shape; Decision 3's arithmetic fix flows through automatically, but nothing proves it. Note this rule runs only in `checkAll()`, not `check()` — a regression case needs the arch-plan-pair setup. Extend Task 12 with one arch-rule case (or amend the criterion if the scope reduction is intentional).

findings.title: Task 8's "only caller passes a full `SlicePlanEntry`" claim is inaccurate
findings.description: `resolveEntryStatus`'s only caller is `resolveEntryStatusSafe` (WorkflowNavigator.ts:734-742), which forwards its own `entry` parameter typed `Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>` (line 736). Widening only the `Pick` at line 694 as Task 8 instructs makes the call at line 740 a type error (missing `status`) — line 736's `Pick` must be widened too. The "builds clean" success criterion makes this self-correcting, but the task's justification ("widening the `Pick` is a compatible narrowing-relaxation… no other call site breaks") is wrong as written.

findings.title: Commit markers are checklist items, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The commit points (lines 105, 135, 179, 197, and two in Tasks 12–13) are written as `- [ ] Commit:` checklist sub-items rather than plain `**Commit**:` marker lines. Placement is otherwise correct — they sit at working, tested points (after green-test success lines), not after every task and not only at the end. If commit-marker tooling parses the plain-line form, these will not be found.

findings.title: A third `completedSlices === totalSlices` consumer exists beyond the design's "two rules"
findings.description: The slice design states "two rules (`plan-status-vs-entries`, `arch-status-vs-plans`) compute `allComplete`", but `ruleInitiativePlanStatusVsEntries` (lines 981-1003) applies the same arithmetic to initiative plans parsed by the same `parseSlicePlan`, with the same permanent-false-positive shape for a `[~]` entry. Decision 3's parser-level fix covers it automatically, and it is outside the named success criteria, so no task is strictly required — but the design's "two rules" statement is factually undercounted and the rule is untested for the deprecated case.
